newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bomb injures four in Albanian-dominated Kosovo.
newsitem.headline: Bomb injures four in Albanian-dominated Kosovo.

text.p: Four people were injured on Wednesday, police said, when a bomb exploded in the centre of Pristina, capital of the volatile Serbian province of Kosovo where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one.
The blast came as serious unrest continued in neighbouring Albania.
Witnesses said the device was in a garbage container beside the monument of Serbian language reformer Vuk Karadzic, in front of Pristina university's Faculty of Philosophy.
Debris from the blast was strewn up to 100 metres (yards) away, smashing windows in the faculty and surrounding buildings.
Police deactivated a second bomb nearby after it failed to explode, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said.
"...it is supposed that this is yet another terrorist attack directed at jeopardising the University in Pristina and provoking trouble in Kosovo," Tanjug said.
One senior Serbian official told Reuters another bomb, also in a garbage container, went off at the same time in Prizren beside the monument of Serbian King Dusan.
This could not immediately be confirmed and there were no reports of any casualties or damage in the town south of Pristina.

Police sources believe the devices were planted by the clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) which is reported to have been behind guerrilla attacks in Kosovo over the past year in which more than 30 people have died.
The latest attacks follow several quiet weeks in the province, after Serbian police arrested some 70 people in a widely-publicised sweep in January.
The province has since been widely regarded as a powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
The latest violence coincides with preparations for talks on the status of Albanians in Kosovo due to be held between Serbian officials and an ethnic Albanian leader in New York in April.
